title: Variational inference & amortisation
blurb: Choosing $q_\phi$, joint learning of $\theta,\phi$, amortised inference

hook.title: Tailor-made vs the size chart
hook.text: The true posterior is a shape you can't write down. **Variational inference** says: pick a shape you *can* work with (say a Gaussian) and tune its dials until it hugs the true shape as closely as possible. Doing that tuning from scratch for each of a million data points is like hiring a tailor for each customer. **Amortised inference** builds a **size chart**: one network $f_\lambda$ that reads $x$ and instantly outputs good dial settings $\phi$, even for a customer it has never seen.
hook.recall: Remember the tailor vs size chart: VI picks $\phi$ to make $q(z;\phi)$ close to the posterior; amortisation learns one function $x\mapsto\phi$ instead of optimising a new $\phi^i$ per data point.

explore.intro: Two tabs: fit $q$ to a bumpy posterior, then see why amortising helps.
tasks: Start with $\phi_1=-4$, $\phi_2=0.75$ (the “bad” green-style fit). Then try a mean near 2. Compare the ELBOs.
Amortised tab: move the new $x$. Did we run an optimisation for it?
explore.takeaway: Better $q$ ⇒ smaller $D_{KL}(q\|p(z|x))$ ⇒ ELBO closer to $\log p(x)$. Amortised inference learns $f_\lambda:x\mapsto\phi$ (written $q_\phi(z|x)$) and trains $\theta,\phi$ jointly by SGD.

options: Picks $\phi$ so that $q(z;\phi)$ is close to the posterior $p(z|x;\theta)$
questions.explanation: Tune the tractable family until it hugs the intractable posterior.

questions.prompt: $\log p(x)=-7$. For a variational choice $\phi_2$, $D_{KL}(q_{\phi_2}\|p(z|x))=2.5$. What is its ELBO?
questions.explanation: ELBO $=\log p(x)-D_{KL}=-7-2.5=-9.5$, a valid but loose bound.

questions.prompt: Torn-photo example: is $q$ with $\phi_i=0.5$ for every missing pixel a good approximation of $p(x_{top}|x_{bottom})$?
options: No: it ignores the evidence in the visible bottom half
questions.explanation: A good $q$ sets $\phi_i\approx1$ for the pixels that form the top of a “9”.

questions.prompt: *“Because $q_\phi(z|x)$ is a neural network, it must equal the true posterior exactly.”* What’s wrong?
options: It’s still a restricted tractable family (e.g. a Gaussian); the better it matches, the closer the bound, but equality only holds when $q=p(z|x)$
questions.explanation: A size chart gets most customers close, not every customer perfect.
